  <header class="page-intro"><p class="eyebrow">ABOUT ME</p><h1>Research rooted in<br><em>real-world questions.</em></h1><p class="page-intro-lede">I am Fallah Nyumah, a PhD researcher in Forestry at the University of Toronto, working at the intersection of sustainable landscapes, environmental policy, and applied research.</p></header>

Environmental Management · REDD+</strong></div></div>
    <div class="story-main"><h2>About my work</h2><p>My doctoral research investigates how oil palm and rubber plantations in Liberia can remain productive and climate-resilient while accounting for carbon dynamics, environmental impacts, and economic outcomes. I combine process-based modelling, techno-economic analysis, life-cycle assessment, and decision-support methods to evaluate alternative plantation management pathways.</p><p>My background also encompasses tropical forest conservation, participatory forest management, environmental regulation, and climate policy. Previous appointments include the Environmental Protection Agency of Liberia, a remote internship with the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Transparency Division, and university teaching in Liberia and Canada.</p><p>Across these roles, I have used quantitative and qualitative research, survey design, statistical analysis, geospatial tools, and policy communication to connect research evidence with real-world environmental decisions.</p><h2 class="section-subhead">Research and methodological interests</h2><div class="tagline topic-stack"><span class="topic-tag">Tree Crop Plantation Sustainability</span><span class="topic-tag">Tropical Forest Conservation</span><span class="topic-tag">Process-based Modelling</span><span class="topic-tag">Climate Change Adaptation</span><span class="topic-tag">Forest and Environmental Economics</span><span class="topic-tag">Life-cycle Assessment</span><span class="topic-tag">REDD+ and AFOLU</span><span class="topic-tag">Environmental Impact Assessment</span><span class="topic-tag">Survey and Statistical Analysis</span><span class="topic-tag">Grant Writing and Scientific Communication</span><span class="topic-tag">GIS</span><span class="topic-tag">R and Shiny</span></div></div>
  </section>
